titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 15, the hymns (part 3 of 4)
part: Spell 15 — the hymns, part 3 of 4: Ani's hymn to Ra rising and setting, and his prayer to join the spirits and see the god (Plates 20–21)
about: The third part of Spell 15 carries on Ani's hymn to Ra on Plates 20 and 21. Ani greets the sun rising in its horizon as Ra, crossing the sky in its bark and covering millions of river-lengths in a moment, then completing the hours of the night and setting in Nu; he asks to reach the sky of eternity, to be joined with the spirits of the necropolis and to come forth with them to see the god's beauty. A last address praises the god who rises like gold, born of his mother Nut, who makes the towns and temples festive and feeds the ka, and the hymn runs on into the next part. Budge's type is uncertain in many signs here, and the notes say where a reading is doubtful.

sentences.l: O · Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · in · peace · true-of-voice · says · he
sentences.i: O Osiris Ani, true of voice in peace, true of voice! He says:
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i 'O' and ḏd·f 'he says' in red. i is the reed with a man raising one arm (A26, approximate), the call that the previous part ended on. Wsir ꜣny 'Osiris Ani': here the seated man on a chair (A51, approximate) is Ani's classifier. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' (the plinth and the oar) is written twice, before and after m ḥtp 'in peace', where ḥtp is the offering-table alone (R4), with no t or p. ḏd·f is the cobra ḏ, the hand d and ·f.

sentences.l: hail · to-your-face · rise · you · in · horizon · your · as · Ra · resting · upon · Maat
sentences.i: Hail to you! You rise in your horizon as Ra, resting upon Maat.
sentences.n: Ani's speech begins with ind ḥr·k 'hail to you', which the papyrus writes in red. Budge prints ànet'-ḥrà-k as one group (his numeral 16 stands before it); it is split here into ind and ḥr·k, as in the previous part. ind is the reed and the post nḏ (Aa27, approximate); ḥr·k is the face with its stroke and ·k. wbn·k 'you rise' is the chick w, the foot b, water n and the sun, with ·k: a sḏm·f. ꜣḫt·k 'your horizon' is the sun between two hills (N27) with t and a house-like sign (O1, approximate). m rꜥ 'as Ra': r, the arm ꜥ (D36 here, not U15) and the god with the sun-disk. ḥtp ḥr mꜣꜥt 'resting upon Maat': ḥtp (offering-table, t, p) is the stative after rꜥ, 'at rest, content', and ḥr 'upon'; mꜣꜥt is the plinth mꜣꜥ with t and a seated goddess holding an ankh (C10, approximate) as classifier: Maat, right order, the goddess on whom the sun's course rests (Budge: 'stablished by Maāt').

sentences.l: cross · you · the-sky · face · every · (is)-upon · seeing · you
sentences.i: You cross the sky, and every face is watching you.
sentences.n: ḏꜣ·k 'you cross' is a tall tapering sign, the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28, approximate), with ꜣ and a boat as classifier (P1, approximate: a ship with a cabin and curled ends), and ·k: ḏꜣi 'cross (water), ferry over', said of the sun crossing the sky as a boat crosses the river. pt 'the sky' (p, t and the sky). ḥr nb 'every face': the face with its stroke, and nb after a noun, 'every'. ḥr mꜣꜣ·k 'is upon seeing you': the preposition ḥr with the infinitive mꜣꜣ, the eye with the sickle mꜣ (the second ꜣ not written), and ·k as its object: ḥr with an infinitive says what is going on, 'is watching you'.

sentences.l: going · your · (is)-hidden · from · face · their
sentences.i: Your going is hidden from their sight.
sentences.n: šmt·k 'your going' is the pool š with walking legs through it (one sign in the print, the pool-with-legs, coded as the pool N37, approximate, and the legs D54), the owl m, t, the legs again and ·k: the infinitive of šm 'go', spelled as in Spell 147 (Budge: māśemt-k; his numeral 17 stands before it). imn 'hidden' is the reed, the gaming board mn with n, a man crouching behind a wall (A5, approximate) and the roll: the stative after its subject. m ḥr·sn 'from their face': ḥr with its stroke and ·sn (the bolt s, water n and plural strokes); 'their' are the faces of the line before. The sun's path is seen, but not his going.

sentences.l: give · you · yourself · (at)-dawn · at · evening · day
sentences.i: You give yourself at dawn and at evening, day by day(?).
sentences.n: Budge prints ṭā-k-tu as one group; it is split here into di·k 'you give' (the arm holding a loaf, di, approximate, and ·k) and tw 'yourself', the dependent pronoun (t and w) as object: the god gives himself to be seen. dwꜣt 'dawn' is the star dwꜣ, ꜣ, t and the sun as classifier of time: dwꜣyt 'dawn, morning' without its two reeds, a spelling it shares with dwꜣt 'the Duat', from which the sun classifier tells it apart; no m is written before it. mšrw 'evening' (Budge: māśeru) opens with a sign printed as a flat boat-like body with a post at one end and a stick across it (coded P1, approximate), where the previous part has the owl m with an arm joined to it; it is read m with Budge's mā. Then come the hatched rectangle š (N37), r, the lying lion rw with w, and the night sky with a hanging star (N2, approximate). hrw 'day' is the courtyard h (O4), r, the sun and a stroke; Budge supplies '[every]', and no nb is written.

sentences.l: is-firm · the-Sektet-bark · under · Majesty · your
sentences.i: The Sektet-bark is firm beneath Your Majesty.
sentences.n: rwd 'is firm' is r, the hand d, two strokes, the chick w, a looped cord (the bowstring rwḏ, T12, approximate) and the roll (Budge: reṭiu; his numeral 18 stands before it): rwd, the later spelling of rwḏ 'be firm, strong', a verb of quality standing before its subject; the w is printed after the hand, and the two strokes are not read; the bowstring, the sign that itself writes rwḏ, is the classifier. sqdt is the bolt s, a sign coded Aa28 (qd, approximate: a small eared ring), the hand d, a second hand (perhaps for t), a sign coded W24 (approximate; not read), a boat (P1, approximate) and the walking legs: the name of the Sektet-bark, the bark of the evening, here spelled as if from sqdi 'to sail' (Budge: seqṭet); the shapes of the second, fourth and fifth signs are uncertain. ẖr 'under' is the butcher's block ẖr with r. ḥm·k 'your Majesty' is the club ḥm (U36) with a seated wrapped figure (A40, approximate) and ·k: the god himself, carried by his bark.

sentences.l: rays · your · (are)-in · faces
sentences.i: Your rays are on (all) faces;
sentences.n: stwt·k 'your rays' is the pierced skin st (F29), t, w, the sun with hanging rays (N8, approximate), a stroke and ·k, as in the previous part. m ḥrw 'in faces': the face with two strokes, the plural; Budge supplies '[all]'.

sentences.l: not · are-known · they · the-rays(?) · not · is-told · splendour · your
sentences.i: they are not known, (your) rays(?); your splendour cannot be told.
sentences.n: n is the negative arms (D35, approximate) with water n, both times. Budge prints reχ-set as one group; it is split here into rḫ 'know' (the mouth r over the placenta ḫ, with the roll) and st (the bolt s and t), the dependent pronoun 'they' as the subject of the passive sḏm·f, which writes no ending: n rḫ st 'they are not known' (Budge: 'not known are they'). The next word is a single sign that the type does not make clear, an upright through a crossbar with hanging ends (coded U38, the balance, approximate), with a stroke; Budge reads smu with his own (?) and renders 'rays'. Its reading is doubtful, and smw(?) only gives it a place. n smi imw·k 'your splendour is not told': smi 'report, tell' is the bolt s and the milk-jug mi in its net (W19) with the reed, again the passive sḏm·f after n. imw·k is the reed, a flat bar (Aa13, approximate) read im with Budge (àmmu-k, 'thy beams'), the owl m as complement, w, the sun with hanging rays, a stroke and ·k: a word for the god's light, classified with the rays; its exact sense is not known.

morph.gloss: rays (?) (reading of the sign doubtful; Budge: smu(?), 'rays')
splendour, beams (?) (noun; written with the sun's rays as classifier; Budge: àmmu, 'beams')

sentences.l: the-lands · of · the-gods · have-been-seen · together-with(?) · the-colours(?) · of-the-hill-countries · of · Punt · so-that · may-be-reckoned · what-is-hidden
sentences.i: The lands of the gods have been seen, and the colours(?) of the hill-countries of Punt, so that what is hidden may be reckoned(?).
sentences.n: tꜣw 'the lands' is the land sign three times (Budge: taiu; his numeral 19 stands before the word before it). nw, the pot nw with a stroke, is the genitive in the plural, agreeing with tꜣw. mꜣꜣ·n·tw is the eye with the sickle mꜣ (Budge's type sets the sickle above the eye), two vultures ꜣ, water n, and t and w: the passive of the sḏm·n·f, 'have been seen', after its subject (Budge: maa-entu, 'must be looked upon'). ḥr is the face with its stroke, taken as 'together with, besides' (Budge: 'and'). sš is the scribe's outfit (Y3, approximate) with the roll and a stroke: sš 'writing, painting', perhaps the painted colours of the land; Budge reads the sign ān, his old value for it, and renders 'the colours of'. Both words are doubtful. ḫꜣswt is the hill-country sign written three times (N25, approximate), ḫꜣst 'hill-country, foreign land' in the plural (Budge: set, 'the eastern countries'). pwnt 'Punt' is p, the hare wn with n, t and the hill-country sign: the land of incense on the Red Sea, in the east where the sun rises. r sip·tw imn: r with a passive sḏm·f, 'so that … may be', taken with Budge ('for to be computed'); sip 'examine, reckon' is the bolt s, the reed, p, a looped cord (V6, approximate) as classifier, and the t and w of the passive; Budge's numeral 20 stands inside the word, between the cord and the t. imn 'what is hidden' is the participle as a noun, spelled as in line 17.

sentences.l: make · you · being-alone · the-form(?) · of-its-opening(?)
sentences.i: You alone make the form(?) of its opening(?);
sentences.n: ir·k 'you make' is the eye ir and ·k, a sḏm·f. wꜥ·ṯi 'being alone' is the harpoon wꜥ with its stroke and U15 for ꜥ, then the tethering rope ṯ and the reed: the stative of wꜥ 'be one, be alone' with the ending ·ṯi of the 2nd person, which here belongs to 'you', as it should (Budge: uā-θà, 'alone by thyself'). The rest of the clause is obscure. sm, the bolt s and the owl m, is read with Budge (sem, 'form'), a word not otherwise found in the published parts. wn-rꜣ·f is the hare wn with n, the mouth r with its stroke and ·f: as written, 'the opening of its mouth'; Budge prints un-re-f and renders 'its appearance'. The l and i follow Budge's sense with (?); the clause cannot be read with confidence.

morph.gloss: form, image (?) (noun; read with Budge, sem 'form'; doubtful)

sentences.l: forms · your · (are)-upon · Nu
sentences.i: your forms are above Nu.
sentences.n: ḫprw·k is the scarab ḫpr with r and w, a standing mummy (A53, approximate), the roll and a stroke as classifiers, and ·k: ḫprw 'forms, manifestations', the plural noun from ḫpr 'come into being' (Budge: χeperu-k, 'thou comest into existence'). tp 'upon' is the head with its stroke, used as a preposition (Budge: ṭep). nw 'Nu' is the pot nw three times over the sky, three water lines and the seated god: the waters out of which the sun rises.

sentences.l: (iw) · he · (is)-to · go · he · likewise · as · your-going
sentences.i: He shall go even as you go;
sentences.n: iw·f 'he' is the reed, the chick w and ·f; iw with a suffix, r and an infinitive is the future, 'he is to …, he shall …'. Who 'he' is the text does not say; the lines that follow speak of 'your Majesty' in the second person, and 'he' is probably Ani speaking of himself (Budge: 'He, may he progress'). šm·f is spelled like šmt·k in line 17 but without t (Budge's numeral 21 stands before it), and the ·f after it repeats the subject. mitt 'the like, likewise' is the milk-jug mi, t twice and a flat bar with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) as classifier; with r after it, 'like (unto)'. šmt·k 'your going' as in line 17.

sentences.l: not · makes · he · a-stopping · like · Majesty · your · (for)-a-day · little
sentences.i: he makes no halt, like Your Majesty, even for a short day.
sentences.n: n, the negative arms over water n, stands in square brackets in Budge's hieroglyphs: it is his restoration where the papyrus is damaged. ir·n·f is the eye, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·f; n with the sḏm·n·f is the general negative, 'he does not, he cannot' (Budge: àri-nef). ꜣbw 'a stopping' is a sign coded U23 (the chisel, approximate: a small ring with a bar above and below on a long stick), read ꜣb with Budge's āb, with b, w and the sun as classifier: a noun from ꜣb 'cease' (Budge: ābu, 'cessation'). mi ḥm·k 'like your Majesty': ḥm is the club with a stroke and a seated long-wigged figure (A40, approximate). hrw ktt 'a little day', said as an adverb, 'even for a moment': ktt 'little' is k, t twice and the sparrow (G37), the classifier of small things; its feminine ending does not agree with hrw (Budge: ketet). The sun never stops in its course.

sentences.l: hastening · you · going-far · you · (over)-river-lengths · in · millions · (and)-hundreds-of-thousands · (in)-a-moment · little
sentences.i: Hastening and going far, you cross river-lengths by millions and hundreds of thousands in one brief moment.
sentences.n: Two statives with the 2nd person ending, like wꜥ·ṯi in line 20. ḥp·t is the wick ḥ, p, t and the walking legs: taken as a verb of motion ḥpi 'hasten, travel (?)', its ending written with t alone (Budge: ḥept, 'striding'); the verb and the form are doubtful. wꜣ·ti is the looped cord wꜣ (V4, approximate) with ꜣ and w as complements, then a sign that Budge reads θ (a crossbar with a knob at each end and a pendant below: coded U38, approximate; it may be the road with shrubs, the classifier of roads) and the walking legs as classifiers, and a narrow rounded upright (U33, ti, approximate) with the reed for the ending ·ti: wꜣi 'go far' (Budge: uau-θà, 'travelling over'; his numeral 22 stands after the first sign). itrw is the reed, t, r, w, three water lines, a stroke and a canal sign (N23, approximate) with a stroke: the word for 'river' is also the river-length, the Egyptian measure of long distances (Budge: àtru, 'distances'). m ḥḥ ḥfnw 'by millions and hundreds of thousands': ḥḥ is the god with raised arms (C11), the numeral for a million, with two strokes; ḥfnw is the tadpole (I8), the numeral for a hundred thousand, with a stroke. ꜣt šrit 'a little moment', an adverb of time: ꜣt is an animal's head (F9, approximate) with t and the sun as classifier of time; šrit 'little' is the hatched rectangle š (N37), r, the reed, t and the sparrow, the feminine agreeing with ꜣt (Budge: śerà, without the t, which the type sets above the sparrow).

morph.gloss: river; here the river-length, a measure of long distances (noun)

sentences.l: have-done · you · it · have-set · you
sentences.i: You have done it, and you have set.
sentences.n: ir·n·k is the eye ir, the chick w (Budge: àru-nek; not read), the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k. st 'it' is the dependent pronoun, the object: the journey just described. ḥtp·n·k 'you have set': ḥtp, the offering-table with t and p, said of the sun going to rest, with the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k.

sentences.l: have-completed · you · the-hours · of-the-night · likewise
sentences.i: You have brought the hours of the night to their end likewise;
sentences.n: km·n·k is a flat sign with spines at its sloping end, the crocodile skin km (I6, approximate), with m, the roll, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k: km 'complete, bring to an end' (Budge: qam-nek; his numeral 23 stands after the first sign). wnwt 'the hours' is the hare wn with n, the pot nw, t, the star and the sun as classifiers, and a stroke. grḥ 'night' is the jar-stand g (W11, approximate), r, ḥ and the night sky with a hanging star (N2, approximate), a direct genitive after wnwt. mitt 'likewise' as in line 21: the hours of the night are finished as the hours of the day were.

sentences.l: have-passed-through(?) · you · them · have-completed · you · according-to · ordinance · your · the-land-grows-bright
sentences.i: you have passed through(?) them, you have completed (them) according to your ordinance, and the land grows bright.
sentences.n: msms·n·k is a long open sign with a slanted end (coded N36, approximate; no good code) over the bolt s, written twice, the walking legs, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k: read with Budge mes-mes, a doubled verb not otherwise found in the published parts. The legs as classifier point to movement, 'pass through(?)', where Budge renders 'thou dost thyself count'; reading and sense are doubtful. st 'them', the hours. km·n·k as in line 22, with no object written (Budge supplies '[them]'). mi ntꜥ·k 'according to your ordinance': ntꜥ is water n, t, U15 for ꜥ, a stroke and a flat bar with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) as classifier: ntꜥ 'custom, ordinance, the set way of doing' (Budge: entā-k, 'thy statutes'). ḥḏ-tꜣ is the mace ḥḏ and the cobra ḏ printed as one ligature (T3 and I10, approximate), the sun as classifier, and the land sign (N16, approximate): ḥḏ tꜣ 'the land grows bright', the Egyptian way of saying 'dawn', kept as one word as Budge prints it (ḥet'-ta). The night ends and the day begins again.

sentences.l: give · you · yourself · to · work · your(?) · as · Ra · rise · you · in · the-horizon
sentences.i: You give yourself to your work(?) as Ra, and you rise in the horizon.
sentences.n: di·k tw 'you give yourself' as in line 17; Budge again prints ṭā-k-tu as one group, split here (his numeral 24 stands before it). r 'to'. r-ꜥ·k is r, U15 for ꜥ, a stroke and ·k, read with Budge (rā-k, 'thy work') as the noun rꜣ-ꜥ 'activity, work', its rꜣ written with r alone; the word is doubtful. m rꜥ 'as Ra': Ra is spelled here with U15 for ꜥ. wbn·k m ꜣḫt 'you rise in the horizon', as in line 16: the round of the day begins again.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · says · he
sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, says:
sentences.n: Wsir sš ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: sš 'scribe' is the scribe's palette, water-pot and pen (Y3, approximate), Ani's title (Budge reads the sign ān, his old value); ꜣny has a squatting man holding a flail (A52) as classifier. ḏd·f 'he says' is written in red.

sentences.l: adores · he · you · in · shining · your
sentences.i: He adores you in your shining;
sentences.n: What Ani says opens with two sentences about himself in the third person. dwꜣ·f 'he adores' is the star dwꜣ with ꜣ, a man with both arms raised (A28, approximate), the roll and ·f (Budge's numeral 25 stands before it); tw 'you' is the object. psd·k 'your shining', as in the previous part: p, the bolt s, the hand d for ḏ, the sun with hanging rays and ·k (Budge: pesṭ-k); here the infinitive, with ·k as its subject.

sentences.l: says · he · to-you · in · rising · your · in · dawning · your · in · exalting · forms · your
sentences.i: he says to you, at your rising, at your dawning, as he exalts your forms:
sentences.n: ḏd·f 'he says', this time not in red. n·k 'to you' is water n and ·k. m wbn·k 'at your rising' and m dwꜣw·k 'at your dawning': two infinitives or nouns with m, saying when; dwꜣw is the star with ꜣ, w and the sun (Budge: ṭuau-k), the noun dwꜣw 'morning'. m sqꜣ ḫprw·k: sqꜣ 'exalt, make high' is the bolt s, a small triangle q (N29, approximate), ꜣ, a man with both arms raised (A28, approximate) and the roll: the causative of qꜣi 'be high', here the infinitive with its object (Budge: seqa, 'exulting over'). ḫprw·k 'your forms' is the scarab with r, plural strokes and ·k, as in line 20.

sentences.l: appear · you · in · making-great · beauty · your
sentences.i: You appear, making your beauty great.
sentences.n: The words he says to the god begin. ḫꜥ·k 'you appear' is the hill with the rays of the rising sun ḫꜥ (N28), U15 written twice as complement of ꜥ, a flat bar with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) as classifier and ·k (Budge: χāā-k, 'thou art crowned'; his numeral 26 stands before it): ḫꜥ 'appear', said of the sun at its rising and of a king on his throne. sꜥꜣ is the bolt s, a long rod with a lozenge at its end (O29, ꜥꜣ), U15 for ꜥ, ꜣ and the roll: sꜥꜣ 'make great', the causative of ꜥꜣ 'great', here the infinitive with its object (Budge: seāāa, 'the majesty of'). The rod O29 stands in square brackets in Budge's hieroglyphs: it is his restoration where the papyrus is damaged. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is the heart-and-windpipe nfr with a stroke and plural strokes, the abstract plural, and ·k.

sentences.l: hastening(?) · fashion · you · limbs · your · bearing · it · without-(pain?)
sentences.i: Hastening(?), you fashion your limbs, bearing it (the body) without (pain?);
sentences.n: ḥpyw is the wick ḥ, p, two strokes y, w, the roll and a second w (Budge: ḥepiu-u, 'advancing'): taken as a form of the verb ḥpi of line 21, here without the walking legs; the last w is not read, and the form is doubtful. nb·k 'you fashion' is the gold collar nb (S12) with b and U15 as classifier, and ·k: nbi 'mould, fashion', the goldsmith's word (Budge: nub-k). ḥꜥw·k 'your limbs' is ḥ, U15 for ꜥ, a curl of flesh (F51, approximate), plural strokes and ·k. Budge prints messu as one group; it is split here into ms, the three fox-skins ms with s, and sw, the sedge sw (M23, approximate) with w: the dependent pronoun 'it' as the object of ms 'giving birth', the body as one (Budge: 'bringing them forth'). iwty 'without' is the negative arms (D35, approximate), t, two strokes y and the sparrow (G37), the negative relative 'who has not'. Budge reads àt men, 'painlessly', but no sign for mn 'pain' is printed: the sparrow, classifier of bad and small things, is the only trace of a noun after iwty, and either the noun has been left out or iwty stands alone. The sun makes and bears his own body.

sentences.l: is-born · he · as · Ra · rising · in · the-sky
sentences.i: he is born as Ra, rising in the sky.
sentences.n: ms·tw·f is ms with s, the t and w of the passive and ·f: 'he is born' (Budge: mestu-f, 'born is he'); the same signs are read mswt·f 'his birth' in line 32, where the genitive n stands before them. The god is spoken of here in the third person. m rꜥ 'as Ra' (Budge's numeral 27 stands before rꜥ). wbn 'rising' is the participle. ḥrt 'the sky, what is above' is the face ḥr with r, t and the sky.

sentences.l: grant · you · may-reach · I · the-sky · of · eternity · (and)-the-desert-place(?) · of · the-favoured-ones
sentences.i: Grant that I may reach the sky of eternity and the desert-place(?) of the favoured ones;
sentences.n: di·k 'may you give', the arm with the loaf and ·k, followed by a sḏm·f: 'grant that I may …'. pḥ·i 'I may reach' is the hindquarters of a lion pḥ (F22, approximate) with the walking legs and ·i. ḥrt nt ḥḥ 'the sky of eternity': nt, the genitive in the feminine, agrees with ḥrt; ḥḥ is the twisted wick ḥ twice with the sun between them, nḥḥ 'eternity' without its first n, as in the previous part. st nt ḥsyw: st is the bolt s, t and the hill-country sign (N25, approximate): 'place' classified as desert, the high desert of the tombs (Budge: set, 'the mountain'). ḥsyw 'the favoured ones' is the wick ḥ, the tall jar ḥs (W14), s, two reeds y, w, a kneeling man (A1; partly hidden in the print, A2 possible) and a stroke: the passive participle of ḥsi 'favour', used as a noun, the blessed dead; Budge supplies '[thy]'.

sentences.l: may-be-joined · I · with · the-spirits · noble · excellent · of · the-necropolis
sentences.i: may I be joined with the noble and excellent spirits of the necropolis.
sentences.n: smꜣ·i is the lungs and windpipe smꜣ (F36) with ꜣ, the roll and ·i: smꜣ 'unite, join', a sḏm·f for a wish (Budge: sama-à). m ꜣḫw 'with the spirits' (Budge's numeral 28 stands before m): the crested ibis ꜣḫ with ḫ, w, a squatting figure with a flail (A52) and a stroke: the transfigured dead. šps 'noble' is a noble seated on a chair (A51, approximate) with s, and two strokes and a flat roll (Y1) as classifiers; iqr 'excellent' is the reed, a small triangle q (N29, approximate), r, the roll and a stroke: two adjectives after ꜣḫw, their plural endings unwritten. nw, the genitive in the plural, and ẖrt-nṯr 'the necropolis', with the flag nṯr written first out of respect, and r and the butcher's block ẖr printed with it as one group (the r approximate).

morph.gloss: to unite, join; (passive) to be joined (verb; written with the lungs and windpipe)

sentences.l: may-come-forth · I · with · them · to · see · beauty · your · (when)-rise · you
sentences.i: May I come forth with them to see your beauty when you rise.
sentences.n: pr·i 'may I come forth' is the house pr with r, the walking legs and ·i, a wish. ḥnꜥ·sn 'with them' is ḥ, water n, U15 for ꜥ and ·sn (the bolt s, water n and plural strokes). r mꜣꜣ 'to see': the eye with the sickle and two vultures. nfrw·k 'your beauty' is the last word before Budge's heading PLATE XXI; wbn·k stands at the head of the next plate, still in line 28 (the numeral 29 follows it): a sḏm·f that says when, 'as you rise' (Budge: '[as] thou shinest').

sentences.l: (at)-evening · have-traversed · you · mother · your · Nut
sentences.i: At evening you have passed through your mother Nut.
sentences.n: mšrw 'evening' (Budge's numeral 29 stands before it) opens with the same boat-like sign as in line 17 (P1, approximate), read m with Budge's mā; no preposition is written before it. nmi·n·k 'you have traversed' is water n, a tall slanting rod (T34, nm, approximate) with m, the reed, a step-shaped sign (O38, approximate) and the walking legs as classifiers, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k (Budge: nemmà-nek, 'thou goest'); nmi takes the place crossed as its object. mwt·k 'your mother' is the vulture mwt with t and ·k. nwt 'Nut' is written with the crossed circle, the town sign niwt (O49), read for its sounds, where Nut is elsewhere written with the pot nw; then t, a stroke and the sky. Budge's type prints the town sign, as in niwwt 'towns' in line 33. Nut, the sky, receives the sun at evening and bears him again at dawn.

sentences.l: give · you · (your)-face · to · the-right
sentences.i: You set (your) face to the right, to the west;
sentences.n: di·k ḥr r 'you set the face towards': rdi ḥr r is the idiom 'turn the face to'. ḥr is the face with its stroke. Budge prints (sic) over the group and reads ḥrà-[k], supplying the k in brackets in his transliteration only: no k is printed, and 'your' is understood. The mouth r after the face, which Budge's group takes in, is split off here as the preposition r of the idiom. wnmy is a flower on a stem (M42, wn, approximate; the emblem of the West, R14, is possible in shape), the owl m, two strokes y and a low curled sign (coded U15, approximate) as classifier: wnmy 'right (side)' (Budge: unemi, 'the west'). The Egyptians faced south to orient themselves, so that the right hand is the west, where the sun sets.

sentences.l: arms-two · my · (are)-in · adoration · of · setting · your · as · a-living-one
sentences.i: my two arms are in adoration of your setting as one who lives.
sentences.n: ꜥwy·i 'my two arms' is the arm twice with a stroke between them, two strokes y, w and ·i (a kneeling man with an arm raised): the dual (Budge: āāiu-à). m iꜣw 'in adoration' is the reed, ꜣ, w, a man with both arms raised (A28, approximate), the roll and a stroke (Budge's numeral 30 follows it). n ḥtp·k: water n alone, taken as the genitive, 'of your setting' (Budge: 'when thou settest'). m ꜥnḫ 'as a living one': the ankh with n and ḫ. The sun goes down alive and does not die in the west.

sentences.l: you · indeed · who-made · eternity
sentences.i: It is you, indeed, who made eternity.
sentences.n: ntk is ir ḥḥ: ntk 'you' with a participle after it, 'it is you who …', strengthened by is 'indeed' (the reed and the folded cloth s), as at the end of the previous part. ir is the eye alone, the participle of iri 'make'. ḥḥ is nḥḥ 'eternity', the wick ḥ twice with the sun, as in line 27.

sentences.l: one-adores · (you) · setting · your · in · Nu
sentences.i: You are adored when you set in Nu.
sentences.n: dwꜣ·tw is the star with ꜣ, a man with both arms raised (A28, approximate), the roll, and the t and w of the passive: 'one adores, (you) are adored' (Budge prints ṭua-tu as one group, 'art adored thou'); the god is understood as the subject. ḥtp·k 'your setting' says when. nw 'Nu' as in line 20: the sun goes down into the waters it rose from.

sentences.l: have-placed · I · you · in · heart · my · without · failing
sentences.i: I have set you in my heart, without failing,
sentences.n: di·i tw 'I have placed you': the giving arm with ·i, a sḏm·f here of a thing done, and tw 'you' (Budge: ṭā-à tu). ib·i 'my heart' is the heart-jar with its stroke and ·i. iwty 'without' is a flat bar with a raised bump in the middle (coded Aa13, approximate; no exact code), t, two strokes y and a small bird with a raised tail (G37, approximate); Budge's numeral 31 is printed inside the word, before the bird. bgꜣy is the foot b, a jar-stand g (W11, approximate; Budge's ḳ), ꜣ, two reeds y and a seated man slumped with his arms drawn in (A7, approximate), the classifier of weariness: bgꜣ 'weariness, failing' (Budge: beḳai, 'wavering').

sentences.l: more-divine · than · the-gods
sentences.i: (you who are) more divine than the gods!
sentences.n: nṯry is the flag nṯr with t (for ṯ) and r as complements, two strokes y and the roll: the adjective nṯry 'divine', with r 'than' for the comparative, as with ꜣḫ r nṯrw in the previous part (Budge: neteri, 'O mightier'). nṯrw is the flag three times.

sentences.l: the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · says · he
sentences.i: The Osiris Ani, true of voice, says:
sentences.n: Wsir ꜣny mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: ꜣny here with a kneeling man raising an arm (A1) as classifier. ḏd·f is written in red. A new address begins.

sentences.l: praise · to-you · who-rises · as · gold
sentences.i: Praise to you, who rises like gold,
sentences.n: Budge prints àau-nek as one group; it is split here into iꜣw 'praise', spelled as in line 29, and n·k 'to you' (water n and ·k). wbn 'who rises' is the participle, printed in the order chick w, sun, foot b, water n, the sun set early in the group (Budge's numeral 32 follows it). m nbw 'as gold': the collar nbw (S12) with a small ring (N33, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers of metal: the sun shines like gold.

sentences.l: who-brightens · the-Two-Lands · on · the-day · of · birth · his
sentences.i: who brightens the Two Lands on the day of his birth.
sentences.n: sḥḏ 'who brightens' is the bolt s, the mace ḥḏ (T3, approximate) with the cobra ḏ, and the sun with rays curled inside the cobra's body: the participle of the causative sḥḏ (Budge: seḥet', 'illumining'). tꜣwy 'the Two Lands' is the land sign twice. m hrw n mswt·f 'on the day of his birth': hrw with r, w, the sun and a stroke; mswt 'birth' is ms with s, t, w and ·f (Budge: mestu-f). The god is again 'he' for a moment: each sunrise is his birthday.

sentences.l: has-borne · you · mother · your · upon · (her)-hand
sentences.i: Your mother has given birth to you upon (her) hand;
sentences.n: Budge prints mes-entu as one group; it is split here into ms·n, ms with s and the n of the sḏm·n·f, and tw 'you', the dependent pronoun as object, which stands before the noun subject mwt·k 'your mother', as Egyptian word order requires. mwt·k is the vulture mwt with t, an egg (H8) and a cobra (I12) as classifiers of the female, and ·k. ḥr ḏrt 'upon the hand': ḏrt 'hand' is the hand with t and a stroke (Budge: ṭet); no 'her' is written (Budge supplies it), and the sense of the phrase is not certain.

sentences.l: have-illumined · you · the-circuit · of-the-Disk
sentences.i: you have lit up the circuit of the Disk.
sentences.n: sḥḏ·n·k is s, the mace and the cobra printed as one ligature (T3, approximate, and I10), the plain sun, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·k (Budge: seḥet'-nek). šnw 'circuit' is the cord šn (V7, approximate) with water n twice and a long ring with a tie at one end (V10, approximate; the šn-ring V9 would be expected) as classifier (Budge: śen, 'the orbit'). iṯn 'the Disk' is the reed, the tethering rope ṯ written for t, water n, the sun and the seated god (Budge: àθen), a direct genitive after šnw; Budge's numeral 33 follows it. The sun lights the round it travels.

sentences.l: brightener · great · who-rises · in · Nu
sentences.i: Great brightener, who rises in Nu,
sentences.n: sḥḏ is spelled as in line 32, with a stroke: the participle used as a noun, 'the one who brightens' (Budge: seḥet', 'Light'), with wr 'great' (the swallow wr with r) after it. wbn m nw 'who rises in Nu': the participle and Nu as in line 20.

sentences.l: who-raises-up · kin(?) · his · with · the-flood
sentences.i: who raises up his kin(?) with the flood,
sentences.n: ṯsw is the knot ṯs (S24) over the bolt s, the curl w and U15 as classifier: the participle of ṯs 'tie; raise up' (Budge: θesu, 'strengthening'). mhꜣyw·f opens with the same boat-like sign as mšrw (P1, approximate), read m with Budge's mā, then the courtyard h, ꜣ, two reeds y, w, a long flat bar (Y1, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, and ·f: taken as mhꜣyw 'kinsfolk, family' (Budge: māḥaiu-f, 'his generations of men'); the word and its first sign are doubtful. m ḥbbt 'with the flood' is the wick ḥ, the foot b twice, t and three water lines: ḥbbt 'flood water, the water of the inundation' (Budge: ḥebebet, 'the Nile-flood'). The sun's coming brings the flood that feeds the land.

sentences.l: who-makes-festive · the-councils(?) · all · towns · all · temples · all · (which-are)-splendid(?) · through · beauty · your
sentences.i: who makes festive all the councils(?), all the towns and all the temples, which are splendid(?) through your beauty,
sentences.n: sḥb is s, ḥ, b and the alabaster basin ḥb (W3, approximate) over the sun: the causative of ḥb 'festival', 'who makes festive' (Budge: seḥeb). ḏꜣḏꜣwt: only a bar with three short ticks (coded Aa8, approximate), t and plural strokes are printed (Budge: t'at'at, 'the countries'); read with Budge as ḏꜣḏꜣt 'council, tribunal' in the plural, the courts of the gods(?); the sign and the word are doubtful. nb 'all', the basket after it, stands in square brackets in Budge's hieroglyphs: it is his restoration where the papyrus is damaged. niwwt 'towns' is the crossed town sign with t and plural strokes (Budge's numeral 34 follows). pryt is the house pr with r, two reeds y, t and a second house as classifier, with a stroke: a plural of pr 'house', 'temples' (Budge: perit). nb follows each noun, without the feminine ending. ꜣḫw m nfrw·k: no crested ibis is printed; the signs are the placenta ḫ, a flat arm (D36, approximate) and w, with the roll. They are read with Budge (χu) as ꜣḫw 'effective, splendid', the ibis left out, a stative after the nouns; ḫwi 'protect' ('protected by your beauty') would also fit the signs, and the reading is doubtful.

morph.gloss: councils, courts (?) (here written with one sign; Budge: t'at'at, 'the countries')
houses, temples (plural of pr 'house'; Budge: perit, 'temples')

sentences.l: who-lifts-up · ka · your · with · food · (and)-provisions
sentences.i: who lifts up your ka with food and provisions.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ḏfḏf, the cobra and the viper twice; read ḏfꜣw 'provisions'. wṯsw is the chick w, the knot ṯs over s, the curl w, a post with a hooked top and a slanting foot (coded U39, the support, approximate) and U15 as classifiers: wṯs 'raise up, lift, support', the participle (Budge: uθesu, 'supporting'). kꜣ·k 'your ka' is the raised arms kꜣ with a stroke and ·k. m ḥw ḏfꜣw 'with food and provisions': ḥw is the wick ḥ, w, a long flat bar (Y1, approximate) and a bar with a tuft (Aa13, approximate) with a stroke as classifiers: ḥw 'food, plenty' (Budge: ḥu, 'meats'). In ḏfꜣw, after the doubled ḏf come a long-necked bird (G39, approximate; G38 possible), read ꜣ as in the hymn to Ra, and a rounded loaf with hatching (X4, approximate) with plural strokes as classifiers (Budge: t'eft'ef, 'tchefau food'). The hymn runs on in the next part with a list of the god's epithets.

morph.gloss: food, plenty, provisions (noun; often paired with ḏfꜣw)
